items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: And Peckin' Joe -- I called him good buddy, too, you see

ctx.x: Well, I must agree with that question. It's a very good question, because they were -- I'd say we were all in the same parade. The tap dancers were the tap dancers, you see, and it was just their student body, you see, and they all tried to graduate, you know, or enlarge their degrees, see.

And Peckin' Joe -- I called him good buddy, too, you see, because he was a rapid tapper, see, he wouldn't have it -- he did acrobatics, you know, and we called him -- the acrobat calls it aerials, but he featured his feet, you know. Just the sound of rapid tap because it was -- it was really taken from Pretty Foot, which was some kind of walking that Walter Beatty Bailey used to do -- Pretty Foot. He was proud because he had -- his fiance had accepted him, you know, and had named the day, so he Pretty Foot -- he…
We did do a Pretty Foot, didn't we?
